content_of_post_to_comment:
We discussed thoroughly what signing up and joining a team meant. We discussed the hard work and we even did some drills and exercises so he could see what was coming. We discussed commitment and what that meant. He insisted that he understood and still wanted to play. We told him there would be no quitting. He was making a commitment to his team and himself that he would show up and show out.

I always pushed and instilled in him: You don’t have to be THE best, I just want you to be YOUR best. I motivate him and tell him how proud I am after practices. He’s not meshing with his team. He’s too shy and will not take any of my tips to join the crowd. He insists he’s not good enough, this isn’t for him, he’s always last (He is, he inherited my weight issues so he’s big like me and slow). I tell him it will get better with time. That he’s spending too much time focusing in the negative so that’s all he’ll find, and to try and find ONE thing he likes. But still, every practice he tries quitting or not going. But we make him. Is there anything I can try to make this experience better for him? Or does it just have to suck and be a life lesson? Making him go kills me, but I have to.

Any advice?
